From d4b69a6186b215d2dc1ebcab965ed88e8d41768d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Joshua Rogers <linux@joshua.hu>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 10:05:33 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] SUNRPC: svcauth_gss: avoid NULL deref on zero length
 gss_token in gss_read_proxy_verf

A zero length gss_token results in pages == 0 and in_token->pages[0]
is NULL. The code unconditionally evaluates
page_address(in_token->pages[0]) for the initial memcpy, which can
dereference NULL even when the copy length is 0. Guard the first
memcpy so it only runs when length > 0.

Fixes: 5866efa8cbfb ("SUNRPC: Fix svcauth_gss_proxy_init()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Joshua Rogers <linux@joshua.hu>
Signed-off-by: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>

diff --git a/net/sunrpc/auth_gss/svcauth_gss.c b/net/sunrpc/auth_gss/svcauth_gss.c
index a8ec30759a18..e2f0df8cdaa6 100644
--- a/net/sunrpc/auth_gss/svcauth_gss.c
+++ b/net/sunrpc/auth_gss/svcauth_gss.c
@@ -1083,7 +1083,8 @@ static int gss_read_proxy_verf(struct svc_rqst *rqstp,
 	}
 
 	length = min_t(unsigned int, inlen, (char *)xdr->end - (char *)xdr->p);
-	memcpy(page_address(in_token->pages[0]), xdr->p, length);
+	if (length)
+		memcpy(page_address(in_token->pages[0]), xdr->p, length);
 	inlen -= length;
 
 	to_offs = length;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the `gss_read_proxy_verf` function within `net/sunrpc/auth_gss/svcauth_gss.c`.

### Changes per File

**`net/sunrpc/auth_gss/svcauth_gss.c`**  
- In the `gss_read_proxy_verf` function, added a conditional check (`if (length)`) before the `memcpy` call that copies data from `xdr->p` to `in_token->pages[0]`.  
- The original code unconditionally called `memcpy`, leading to a NULL dereference when `gss_token` had zero length (causing `pages == 0` and `in_token->pages[0] == NULL`).  
- The fix ensures the memory copy only occurs when `length > 0`, avoiding access to the potentially NULL page pointer.

### Relationship Between Modifications

- The single change in the one file directly addresses the core issue: a zero-length `gss_token` would result in `length = 0`, but the old code still attempted to call `page_address(in_token->pages[0])` for the `memcpy` source/destination.  
- By guarding the `memcpy` with a length check, the patch prevents the invalid memory access while preserving the correct behavior for non‑zero length tokens. No other files or functions are affected.

Root cause:
When a zero-length gss_token is received, `pages` is set to 0 and `in_token->pages[0]` is NULL. The code unconditionally calls `page_address(in_token->pages[0])` in the `memcpy` call, leading to a NULL pointer dereference even though the copy length is zero. The missing length check before accessing the page pointer causes the bug.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
memcpy(page_address(in_token->pages[0]), xdr->p, length);
Reason:
When `inlen` is zero, `pages` is zero and `in_token->pages[0]` is NULL. The `memcpy` call unconditionally evaluates `page_address(in_token->pages[0])`, causing a NULL pointer dereference even though `length` (derived from `inlen`) is zero. The missing guard before accessing the page pointer allows the bug.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (length)
	memcpy(page_address(in_token->pages[0]), xdr->p, length);
Reason:
The added `if (length)` check ensures that the `memcpy` is only executed when there is actual data to copy. When `inlen` is zero, `length` is zero, so the problematic `page_address` call is skipped, preventing the NULL dereference. This is the minimal safe guard.

	inlen -= length;

	to_offs = length;
	from_offs = rqstp->rq_arg.page_base;
